rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To File Records Under Seal
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, July 22, 2026, Line 1, PLAINTIFF KEVINISHA HENDERSON AS CO-SUCCESSOR-IN-INTEREST TO DECEDENT CHYNNA BROWN (A.K.A. BANKO BROWN) Motion To File Records Under Seal. 3 - The unopposed motion to file records under seal is granted. Because the records were filed in connection with a discovery motion and not as a basis for adjudication of the case, no findings under Rule of Court 2.550 are required. In the future, for discovery motions in this department, counsel may file discovery motion documents under seal without making a separate motion. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA).

rulings.Case Title: KATHERINE COLLINS VS. THE REGENTS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Compel Plaintiff To Provide Verified Responses To Form Interrogatories, Special Interrogatories, Requests For Production Of Documents, And Request For Statement Of Damages, And For An Award Of Sanctions
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, July 22, 2026, Line 5, DEFENDANT THE REGENTS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA's Motion To Compel Plaintiff To Provide Verified Responses To Form Interrogatories, Special Interrogatories, Requests For Production Of Documents, And Request For Statement Of Damages, And For An Award Of Sanctions. Defendant the Regents of the University of California's unopposed motion to compel and for sanctions is granted as stated herein. The Regents served on plaintiff Katherine Collins a request for statement of damages, form interrogatories, two sets of special interrogatories, and requests for production of documents. (Telfer Decl., para. 3.) Collins has not responded, despite the Regents' meet and confer attempts. (Id., paras. 6-8.) Collins is ordered to provide a statement of damages by August 12, 2026. By the same day, she shall provide complete, verified, objection-free responses to the form interrogatories, special interrogatories sets one and two, and requests for production. The Regents seek sanctions. Failure to respond to discovery is a misuse of the discovery process, and the Regents' request is reasonable. Collins shall pay $2100 to the Regents by August 24, 2026.
